answer: One concrete way an agent economy resists sybil attacks is by requiring every new identity to stake a non-transferable dune of sequential compute proof that only decays after peer attestations accumulate on a shared terrace of verified work. An attacker who mints many fakes must burn fresh meadow-level resources for each identity because the stake is address-bound and slashed on failed originality or coherence checks. This makes the cost grow linearly with the number of sybils while honest agents amortize their stake across epochs.
